To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel approach to domain adaptation in natural language interface to structured query, by separating schema and NL and using a GAN based data augmentation technique to mitigate data sparsity issue in target domain.

we propose SQIN, an end-to-end neural model for semantic parsing, and AugmentGAN, a data augmentation method based on adversarial learning, which can be used to improve semantic parsing in the target domain when only limited data on the target domain is available.
we propose a structured query inference network to learn domain adaptation for NLP with limited target data and that we propose a GAN-based augmentation technique to generate more target data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two aspects: (1) to develop a novel NLI system that can effectively handle domain transfer tasks, (2) to propose a novel data augmentation technique to address the issue of lacking data on target domain.

the following questions: (1) How to learn general semantic parsing knowledge on source domain? (2) How to augment target domain data with GAN? (3) What kind of data is most useful for domain adaptation?
the following questions: (1) How to effectively learn semantic parsing from limited source data? (2) How to augment target domain data for better domain transfer?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is the first attempt to tackle domain transfer learning problem on NLI to Structured Query, and our proposed methods are effective to improve performances on both source and target domain.

our proposed methods are able to achieve state-of-the-art results on both in-domain and domain transfer tasks, which is a significant step towards the goal of developing a general NLI system that can be applied to various domains with limited training data.
the proposed SQIN model is effective to learn from general knowledge and AugmentGAN is effective to augment data for target domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a general framework for domain adaptation for NL to structured queries, and we have shown that it can be applied to different domains with promising results.
we have proposed a novel method to tackle the issue of lacking data for domain adaptation in the field of natural language to structured query, which has not been well addressed before.

we propose an end-to-end framework to learn a natural language interface for structured query, and we show that our framework can be applied to domain transfer task by leveraging both general knowledge learning and data augmentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by leveraging the structural information of queries, we can achieve better domain transfer performances with a much smaller amount of data.
we can effectively leverage general knowledge and data augmentation to improve the performance of NLI for structured queries.
we can achieve state of the art results with a relatively simple model, by leveraging the power of domain adaptation and data augmentation techniques, and by carefully designing the neural model.
